```mermaid
    ServerRecvReq --> CheckServID{Server-ID<br/>Matches This?}
    CheckServID -->|No| DropPacket
    CheckServID -->|Yes| ValidateReqIP[Validate Requested IP]
    
    ValidateReqIP --> CheckReqValid{IP Valid<br/>and Available?}
    CheckReqValid -->|No| SendNAK[Send DHCPNAK]
    CheckReqValid -->|Yes| CheckOldLease{Different IP<br/>Had Old Lease?}
    
    CheckOldLease -->|Yes| PruneOld[lease_prune<br/>Remove Old Lease]
    CheckOldLease -->|No| CreateLease[Create/Update Lease]
    PruneOld --> CreateLease
    
    CreateLease --> PersistLease[lease_update_file<br/>Write to Disk]
    PersistLease --> RegisterDNS[lease_update_dns<br/>Register Hostname]
    RegisterDNS --> QueueScript[queue_script<br/>Execute Lease Script<br/>ACTION=add]
    
    QueueScript --> ConstructACK[Construct DHCPACK<br/>Confirm yiaddr<br/>Include All Options]
    
    ConstructACK --> SetLeaseTime[Set Lease Time<br/>T1 = 50% of Lease<br/>T2 = 87.5% of Lease]
    SetLeaseTime --> SendACK[Send DHCPACK]
    
    SendACK --> ClientRecvACK[Client: Receive ACK]
    ClientRecvACK --> ClientBound[Client: BOUND State<br/>Configure Interface<br/>Use Assigned IP]
    
    ClientBound --> WaitT1[Wait Until T1<br/>50% of Lease Time]
    WaitT1 --> ClientRenew[Client: RENEWING State<br/>Unicast DHCPREQUEST<br/>to Original Server]
    
    ClientRenew --> ServerRecvRenew[Server: Receive REQUEST<br/>RENEWING State]
    ServerRecvRenew --> CheckCiaddr{ciaddr<br/>Valid?}
    CheckCiaddr -->|Yes| ExtendLease[Extend Lease Time]
    CheckCiaddr -->|No| SendNAK
    
    ExtendLease --> UpdateLease[Update Lease Database]
    UpdateLease --> SendRenewACK[Send DHCPACK<br/>New Lease Time]
    SendRenewACK --> ClientBound
    
    WaitT1 --> CheckRenewFail{Renewal<br/>Failed?}
    CheckRenewFail -->|No| ClientBound
    CheckRenewFail -->|Yes| WaitT2[Wait Until T2<br/>87.5% of Lease Time]
    
    WaitT2 --> ClientRebind[Client: REBINDING State<br/>Broadcast DHCPREQUEST<br/>to Any Server]
    ClientRebind --> ServerRecvRebind[Any Server: Process<br/>Rebind Request]
    ServerRecvRebind --> CheckCiaddr
    
    SendNAK --> ClientRecvNAK[Client: Receive NAK]
    ClientRecvNAK --> ClientInit[Client: INIT State<br/>Release IP]
    ClientInit --> SendDiscover
    
    DropPacket --> End([Transaction Dropped])
    
    style CheckIgnore fill:#fff4e1
    style CheckAvail fill:#ffe1e1
    style SendNAK fill:#ffe1e1
    style ClientBound fill:#e1ffe1
```

#### 4.4.1.2 DHCPv4 DECLINE Handling

Clients send DHCPDECLINE when they detect an IP address conflict through ARP probing after receiving DHCPACK. This workflow protects against address conflicts and marks problematic addresses as unavailable.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    ClientRecvACK[Client Receives DHCPACK] --> ARPProbe[Client: ARP Probe<br/>for Assigned IP]
    ARPProbe --> CheckConflict{ARP<br/>Response?}
    
    CheckConflict -->|No, Available| UseIP[Client Uses IP Address]
    CheckConflict -->|Yes, Conflict| SendDecline[Client: Send DHCPDECLINE<br/>with requested-ip option]
    
    SendDecline --> ServerRecvDecline[Server: Receive DECLINE]
    ServerRecvDecline --> ExtractIP[Extract requested-ip<br/>and Server-ID]
    
    ExtractIP --> VerifyServID{Server-ID<br/>Matches?}
    VerifyServID -->|No| IgnoreDecline[Ignore Silently]
    VerifyServID -->|Yes| FindLease[Find Lease by IP]
    
    FindLease --> CheckStatic{Static<br/>Reservation?}
    CheckStatic -->|Yes| DisableStatic[Disable Static IP<br/>for DECLINE_BACKOFF<br/>24 hours]
    CheckStatic -->|No| MarkDeclined[Mark IP as Declined]
    
    DisableStatic --> SetBackoff[Set Backoff Timer]
    MarkDeclined --> SetBackoff
    SetBackoff --> PruneLease[lease_prune<br/>Remove Lease]
    
    PruneLease --> UpdateDB[Update Lease Database]
    UpdateDB --> UpdateDNS[Remove from DNS]
    UpdateDNS --> LogDecline[Log: IP Declined<br/>by Client]
    
    LogDecline --> ForceNew[Force Client to Use<br/>Different IP Next Time]
    
    ForceNew --> ClientRetry[Client Retries<br/>New DHCPDISCOVER]
    ClientRetry --> NewCycle[New DHCP Cycle<br/>Different IP Allocated]
    
    UseIP --> NormalOp([Normal Operation])
    IgnoreDecline --> End([Transaction Complete])
    NewCycle --> End
    
    style CheckConflict fill:#fff4e1
    style MarkDeclined fill:#ffe1e1
```

#### 4.4.1.3 DHCPv4 RELEASE Handling

Clients send DHCPRELEASE when voluntarily releasing their IP address, typically during orderly shutdown. This workflow immediately frees the lease for reuse.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    ClientShutdown[Client Orderly Shutdown] --> SendRelease[Client: Send DHCPRELEASE<br/>Unicast to Server]
    
    SendRelease --> ServerRecv[Server: Receive RELEASE]
    ServerRecv --> ExtractCiaddr[Extract ciaddr<br/>and Server-ID]
    
    ExtractCiaddr --> VerifyServID{Server-ID<br/>Matches?}
    VerifyServID -->|No| IgnoreRelease[Ignore Silently]
    VerifyServID -->|Yes| FindLease[Find Lease by ciaddr]
    
    FindLease --> LeaseFound{Lease<br/>Exists?}
    LeaseFound -->|No| IgnoreRelease
    LeaseFound -->|Yes| VerifyMAC{MAC<br/>Address Match?}
    
    VerifyMAC -->|No| IgnoreRelease
    VerifyMAC -->|Yes| PruneLease[lease_prune<br/>Remove Lease from Database]
    
    PruneLease --> UpdateFile[Update Lease File<br/>Remove Entry]
    UpdateFile --> UpdateDNS[Remove DNS Entry<br/>for Hostname]
    UpdateDNS --> ExecScript[queue_script<br/>Execute Script<br/>ACTION=del]
    
    ExecScript --> FreeIP[Mark IP Available<br/>for Reallocation]
    FreeIP --> LogRelease[Log: Lease Released<br/>by Client]
    
    LogRelease --> Complete([Release Complete])
    IgnoreRelease --> Complete
    
    style VerifyServID fill:#fff4e1
    style LeaseFound fill:#fff4e1
    style VerifyMAC fill:#fff4e1
```

### 4.4.2 DHCPv4 Special Features

#### 4.4.2.1 PXE Boot Integration

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    RecvDiscover[Receive DHCPDISCOVER] --> CheckVendor{"Vendor Class<br/>= 'PXEClient'?"}
    CheckVendor -->|No| StandardDHCP[Standard DHCP Processing]
    CheckVendor -->|Yes| ExtractArch[Extract Client Architecture<br/>Option 93]
    
    ExtractArch --> DetectArch{Architecture<br/>Type?}
    DetectArch -->|0| SetX86BIOS[x86 BIOS]
    DetectArch -->|6| SetX64[x86-64]
    DetectArch -->|7| SetEFIx64[EFI x86-64]
    DetectArch -->|9| SetEFIx86[EFI x86]
    DetectArch -->|Other| SetOtherArch[Other Architecture]
    
    SetX86BIOS --> ExtractUUID[Extract PXE UUID<br/>Option 97]
    SetX64 --> ExtractUUID
    SetEFIx64 --> ExtractUUID
    SetEFIx86 --> ExtractUUID
    SetOtherArch --> ExtractUUID
    
    ExtractUUID --> CheckProxyMode{Proxy<br/>Mode?}
    CheckProxyMode -->|Yes| SkipIPAlloc[Skip IP Allocation<br/>Another Server Provides IP]
    CheckProxyMode -->|No| AllocateIP[Standard IP Allocation]
    
    SkipIPAlloc --> SetBootParams[Set Boot Parameters]
    AllocateIP --> SetBootParams
    
    SetBootParams --> SetBootFile[Set Boot Filename<br/>Based on Architecture<br/>dhcp-boot option]
    
    SetBootFile --> SetTFTPServer[Set TFTP Server Address<br/>Option 66]
    SetTFTPServer --> CheckMenu{PXE Menu<br/>Configured?}
    
    CheckMenu -->|Yes| AddPXEMenu[Add PXE Menu Options<br/>pxe-prompt<br/>pxe-service entries]
    CheckMenu -->|No| SendOffer[Send DHCPOFFER/DHCPACK]
    
    AddPXEMenu --> AddPXEOpts[Add PXE Options<br/>Discovery Control<br/>Boot Servers<br/>Boot Menu]
    AddPXEOpts --> SendOffer
    
    SendOffer --> ClientMenu[Client Displays<br/>Boot Menu]
    ClientMenu --> UserSelect[User Selects<br/>Boot Option]
    UserSelect --> SendBootReq[Client: PXE<br/>Boot Server Request]
    
    SendBootReq --> ServerResp[Server: Send<br/>Specific Boot File]
    ServerResp --> TFTPReq[Client: TFTP Request<br/>for Boot File]
    
    StandardDHCP --> End([DHCP Transaction])
    TFTPReq --> End
    
    style CheckVendor fill:#e1f5ff
    style CheckProxyMode fill:#fff4e1
    style ClientMenu fill:#e1ffe1
```

#### 4.4.2.2 Rapid Commit (RFC 4039)

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    RecvDiscover[Receive DHCPDISCOVER<br/>with Rapid Commit Option] --> CheckAuth{Server<br/>Authoritative?}
    
    CheckAuth -->|No| StandardFlow[Standard Four-Way<br/>DISCOVER-OFFER-REQUEST-ACK]
    CheckAuth -->|Yes| CheckEnabled{Rapid Commit<br/>Enabled?}
    
    CheckEnabled -->|No| StandardFlow
    CheckEnabled -->|Yes| AllocateIP[Allocate IP Address]
    
    AllocateIP --> CheckAvail{Address<br/>Available?}
    CheckAvail -->|No| StandardFlow
    CheckAvail -->|Yes| CommitLease[Commit Lease<br/>Immediately]
    
    CommitLease --> CreateDB[Create Lease Database<br/>Entry]
    CreateDB --> RegisterDNS[Register DNS Entry]
    RegisterDNS --> ExecScript[Execute Lease Script<br/>ACTION=add]
    
    ExecScript --> ConstructACK[Construct DHCPACK<br/>Include Rapid Commit Option]
    ConstructACK --> SendACK[Send DHCPACK<br/>Skip OFFER Phase]
    
    SendACK --> ClientBound[Client: BOUND State<br/>Two-Message Exchange<br/>Complete]
    
    StandardFlow --> NormalFlow([Four-Way Exchange])
    ClientBound --> Complete([Rapid Commit Complete])
    
    style CheckAuth fill:#fff4e1
    style CheckAvail fill:#ffe1e1
    style ClientBound fill:#e1ffe1
```

## 4.5 DHCPv6 Lease Management Workflow

### 4.5.1 DHCPv6 Complete Lifecycle

The DHCPv6 lease management workflow implements RFC 3315 with support for stateful (address assignment) and stateless (configuration only) operation modes, coordinating with IPv6 Router Advertisement for unified IPv6 address management.

#### 4.5.1.1 DHCPv6 Full State Machine

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    ClientBoot[IPv6 Client Boot] --> RecvRA[Receive Router Advertisement]
    RecvRA --> CheckFlags{RA Flags?}
    
    CheckFlags -->|M=1| StatefulMode[Stateful DHCPv6 Mode<br/>Get Address from DHCPv6]
    CheckFlags -->|M=0, O=1| StatelessMode[Stateless DHCPv6 Mode<br/>Use SLAAC for Address<br/>Get Config from DHCPv6]
    CheckFlags -->|M=0, O=0| SLAACOnly[SLAAC Only<br/>No DHCPv6]
    
    StatefulMode --> SendSolicit[Client: Multicast DHCP6SOLICIT<br/>to ff02::1:2 Port 547]
    StatelessMode --> SendInfo[Client: Send<br/>DHCP6INFORMATION-REQUEST]
    
    SendSolicit --> ServerRecvSol[Server: Receive SOLICIT]
    ServerRecvSol --> CheckRelay{Relayed<br/>Message?}
    
    CheckRelay -->|Yes| ProcessRelay[Process DHCP6RELAYFORW<br/>Extract link-address<br/>Recursively Unwrap]
    CheckRelay -->|No| DirectConn[Direct Connection]
    
    ProcessRelay --> ExtractDUID[Extract Client DUID<br/>Mandatory in DHCPv6]
    DirectConn --> ExtractDUID
    
    ExtractDUID --> ParseIA[Parse Identity Association<br/>IA_NA, IA_TA, or IA_PD<br/>Extract IAID]
    
    ParseIA --> ExtractRequested[Extract Requested<br/>IPv6 Addresses]
    ExtractRequested --> CheckRapid{Rapid Commit<br/>Option?}
    
    CheckRapid -->|Yes, Enabled| SkipAdv[Skip ADVERTISE<br/>Go to REPLY]
    CheckRapid -->|No| AddrSelect[Address Selection]
    
    AddrSelect --> ResetUsed[Reset Lease USED Flags]
    ResetUsed --> CheckEachIA[For Each IA in Request]
    
    CheckEachIA --> CheckReqAddr{Requested<br/>Addresses Valid?}
    CheckReqAddr -->|Yes| OfferReq[Offer Requested Addresses]
    CheckReqAddr -->|No| CheckConfig{Configured<br/>Addresses?}
    
    CheckConfig -->|Yes| OfferConfig[Offer Configured Addresses]
    CheckConfig -->|No| CheckExisting{Existing<br/>Leases?}
    
    CheckExisting -->|Yes| OfferExisting[Offer Existing Leases]
    CheckExisting -->|No| AllocateNew[Allocate New Addresses<br/>from Available Ranges]
    
    OfferReq --> CheckMore{More IAs?}
    OfferConfig --> CheckMore
    OfferExisting --> CheckMore
    AllocateNew --> CheckMore
    
    CheckMore -->|Yes| CheckEachIA
    CheckMore -->|No| CheckAvailable{Addresses<br/>Available?}
    
    CheckAvailable -->|No| NoAddrs[Add STATUS_CODE<br/>NoAddrsAvail]
    CheckAvailable -->|Yes| ConstructAdv[Construct DHCP6ADVERTISE]
    
    ConstructAdv --> AddIA[Add IA with<br/>Offered Addresses]
    AddIA --> SetLifetime[Set Preferred Lifetime<br/>Set Valid Lifetime]
    SetLifetime --> AddDNS[Add DNS Servers<br/>Domain Search List]
    AddDNS --> CheckAuth{Server<br/>Authoritative?}
    
    CheckAuth -->|Yes| SetPref[Set Preference<br/>Option to 255]
    CheckAuth -->|No| AddStatus[Add STATUS_CODE Success]
    SetPref --> AddStatus
    
    AddStatus --> SendAdv[Send DHCP6ADVERTISE<br/>Unicast or via Relay]
    NoAddrs --> SendAdv
    
    SendAdv --> ClientRecvAdv[Client: Receive ADVERTISE]
    ClientRecvAdv --> ClientSelectSrv{Select<br/>Server?}
    
    ClientSelectSrv -->|Other Server| WaitMoreAdv[Wait for More Advertise]
    ClientSelectSrv -->|This Server| SendRequest[Client: Unicast<br/>DHCP6REQUEST to Server]
    
    SendRequest --> ServerRecvReq[Server: Receive REQUEST]
    SkipAdv --> ServerRecvReq
    
    ServerRecvReq --> ValidateDUID{Server DUID<br/>Matches?}
    ValidateDUID -->|No| DropPacket[Drop Packet Silently]
    ValidateDUID -->|Yes| ExtractReqIA[Extract Requested IAs<br/>and Addresses]
    
    ExtractReqIA --> ValidateAddrs[Validate Addresses<br/>Appropriate for Client]
    ValidateAddrs --> CheckAddrAvail{Addresses<br/>Available?}
    
    CheckAddrAvail -->|No| SendStatusFail[Send REPLY with<br/>STATUS_CODE Failure]
    CheckAddrAvail -->|Yes| CreateLease[Create or Update<br/>Lease in Database]
    
    CreateLease --> SetExpiry[Set Expiration<br/>Based on Valid Lifetime]
    SetExpiry --> RegisterHost[Register Hostname<br/>in DNS if Provided]
    RegisterHost --> MarkUsed[Mark Context as USED]
    MarkUsed --> ConstructReply[Construct DHCP6REPLY]
    
    ConstructReply --> ConfirmIA[Confirm IA with<br/>Assigned Addresses]
    ConfirmIA --> SetT1T2[Set T1 = 50% of Preferred<br/>Set T2 = 80% of Preferred]
    SetT1T2 --> IncludeOpts[Include All Requested Options]
    IncludeOpts --> AddSuccessStatus[Add STATUS_CODE Success]
    
    AddSuccessStatus --> ExecScript[queue_script<br/>ACTION=add<br/>Pass DUID, IAID, Addresses]
    ExecScript --> SendReply[Send DHCP6REPLY]
    
    SendReply --> ClientRecvReply[Client: Receive REPLY]
    ClientRecvReply --> ClientBound[Client: BOUND State<br/>Configure Interface<br/>Use Assigned Addresses]
    
    ClientBound --> WaitT1[Wait Until T1<br/>50% of Preferred Lifetime]
    WaitT1 --> ClientRenew[Client: RENEWING State<br/>Unicast DHCP6RENEW<br/>to Original Server]
    
    ClientRenew --> ServerRecvRenew[Server: Receive RENEW]
    ServerRecvRenew --> ValidateIA{IAs Valid<br/>for Client?}
    
    ValidateIA -->|No| SendStatusFail
    ValidateIA -->|Yes| ExtendLease[Extend Lease Lifetime]
    ExtendLease --> UpdateDB[Update Lease Database]
    UpdateDB --> SendRenewReply[Send DHCP6REPLY<br/>New Lifetimes]
    SendRenewReply --> ClientBound
    
    WaitT1 --> CheckRenewFail{Renewal<br/>Failed?}
    CheckRenewFail -->|No| ClientBound
    CheckRenewFail -->|Yes| WaitT2[Wait Until T2<br/>80% of Preferred Lifetime]
    
    WaitT2 --> ClientRebind[Client: REBINDING State<br/>Multicast DHCP6REBIND<br/>to Any Server]
    ClientRebind --> ServerRecvRebind[Any Server:<br/>Process REBIND]
    ServerRecvRebind --> ValidateIA
    
    SendInfo --> ServerRecvInfo[Server: Receive<br/>INFORMATION-REQUEST]
    ServerRecvInfo --> ConstructInfoReply[Construct DHCP6REPLY<br/>DNS Servers Only<br/>No Address Assignment]
    ConstructInfoReply --> SendInfoReply[Send DHCP6REPLY]
    SendInfoReply --> ClientRecvInfo[Client: Receive Config]
    
    SLAACOnly --> SLAACAddr([Use SLAAC Address])
    DropPacket --> End([Transaction Dropped])
    SendStatusFail --> End
    ClientRecvInfo --> End
    WaitMoreAdv --> End
    
    style CheckFlags fill:#e1f5ff
    style CheckAvailable fill:#ffe1e1
    style ClientBound fill:#e1ffe1
    style StatelessMode fill:#fff4e1
```

#### 4.5.1.2 DHCPv6 RELEASE Handling

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    ClientShutdown[Client Orderly Shutdown] --> SendRelease[Client: Unicast<br/>DHCP6RELEASE to Server]
    
    SendRelease --> ServerRecv[Server: Receive RELEASE]
    ServerRecv --> ValidateDUID{Server DUID<br/>Matches?}
    
    ValidateDUID -->|No| IgnoreRelease[Ignore Silently]
    ValidateDUID -->|Yes| ExtractIA[Extract IAs from Release]
    
    ExtractIA --> ValidateOwnership{IAs Belong<br/>to Client?}
    ValidateOwnership -->|No| SendStatusFail[Send REPLY with<br/>STATUS_CODE NotOnLink]
    ValidateOwnership -->|Yes| RemoveLeases[Remove Leases<br/>from Database]
    
    RemoveLeases --> UpdateDNS[Remove DNS Entries]
    UpdateDNS --> ExecScript[queue_script<br/>ACTION=del<br/>Pass DUID, Addresses]
    
    ExecScript --> ConstructReply[Construct DHCP6REPLY<br/>with STATUS_CODE Success]
    ConstructReply --> SendReply[Send DHCP6REPLY]
    
    SendReply --> FreeAddrs[Mark Addresses Available<br/>for Reallocation]
    FreeAddrs --> LogRelease[Log: IPv6 Leases Released]
    
    LogRelease --> Complete([Release Complete])
    IgnoreRelease --> Complete
    SendStatusFail --> Complete
    
    style ValidateDUID fill:#fff4e1
    style ValidateOwnership fill:#fff4e1
```

### 4.5.2 DHCPv6 Relay Handling

DHCPv6 relay agents forward DHCPv6 messages between clients and servers on different network segments, encapsulating client messages in DHCP6RELAYFORW and server responses in DHCP6RELAYREPL.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    ClientMsg[Client Sends DHCPv6 Message<br/>on Local Segment] --> RelayRecv[Relay Agent Receives]
    RelayRecv --> BuildRelayForw[Construct DHCP6RELAYFORW]
    
    BuildRelayForw --> SetHopCount[Set Hop-Count = 0]
    SetHopCount --> SetLinkAddr[Set link-address from<br/>Receiving Interface]
    SetLinkAddr --> SetPeerAddr[Set peer-address to<br/>Client IPv6 Address]
    SetPeerAddr --> AddClientMAC[Add OPTION6_CLIENT_MAC<br/>RFC 6939]
    
    AddClientMAC --> EncapClient[Encapsulate Client Message<br/>in RELAY_MSG Option]
    EncapClient --> SendToServer[Forward to DHCPv6 Server]
    
    SendToServer --> ServerRecv[Server Receives RELAYFORW]
    ServerRecv --> CheckMsgType{Message Type<br/>RELAYFORW?}
    
    CheckMsgType -->|No| DirectProcess[Process as Direct Client]
    CheckMsgType -->|Yes| ExtractLinkAddr[Extract link-address]
    
    ExtractLinkAddr --> CheckNested{Nested<br/>Relay?}
    CheckNested -->|Yes| RecurseRelay[Recursively Process<br/>Nested RELAYFORW]
    CheckNested -->|No| DetermineContext[Determine Network Context<br/>from link-address]
    
    RecurseRelay --> DetermineContext
    DetermineContext --> ExtractClientMAC[Extract OPTION6_CLIENT_MAC]
    ExtractClientMAC --> ExtractClient[Extract Client Message<br/>from RELAY_MSG]
    
    ExtractClient --> ProcessDHCP6[Process DHCPv6 Request<br/>Standard Handling]
    ProcessDHCP6 --> BuildResponse[Build DHCPv6 Response]
    
    BuildResponse --> BuildRelayRepl[Construct DHCP6RELAYREPL]
    BuildRelayRepl --> CopyHopCount[Copy Hop-Count<br/>from RELAYFORW]
    CopyHopCount --> CopyLinkAddr[Copy link-address<br/>from RELAYFORW]
    CopyLinkAddr --> CopyPeerAddr[Copy peer-address<br/>from RELAYFORW]
    
    CopyPeerAddr --> EncapResponse[Encapsulate Server Response<br/>in RELAY_MSG Option]
    EncapResponse --> SendToRelay[Send RELAYREPL to<br/>Relay Agent]
    
    SendToRelay --> RelayRecvRepl[Relay Agent Receives RELAYREPL]
    RelayRecvRepl --> UnwrapRelay[Unwrap RELAY_MSG]
    UnwrapRelay --> ForwardClient[Forward to Client<br/>at peer-address]
    
    ForwardClient --> ClientRecv[Client Receives Response]
    DirectProcess --> ClientRecv
    
    style CheckMsgType fill:#fff4e1
    style CheckNested fill:#e1f5ff
```

## 4.6 Network Boot and TFTP Workflows

### 4.6.1 PXE Boot Complete Sequence

The PXE (Preboot Execution Environment) boot workflow enables diskless workstations and thin clients to boot operating systems over the network through coordinated DHCP and TFTP operations.

#### 4.6.1.1 PXE Detection and Boot File Selection

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    ClientPXE[PXE Client Boot ROM] --> SendDiscover[Broadcast DHCPDISCOVER<br/>with PXE Vendor Class]
    
    SendDiscover --> ServerRecv[Server Receives DISCOVER]
    ServerRecv --> CheckVendor{"Vendor Class<br/>= PXEClient?"}
    
    CheckVendor -->|No| StandardDHCP[Standard DHCP Flow]
    CheckVendor -->|Yes| ExtractArch[Extract Architecture<br/>from Option 93]
    
    ExtractArch --> IdentifyArch{Client<br/>Architecture?}
    IdentifyArch -->|0| ArchX86[x86 BIOS]
    IdentifyArch -->|6| ArchX64Legacy[x86-64 Legacy BIOS]
    IdentifyArch -->|7| ArchEFIx64[EFI x86-64]
    IdentifyArch -->|9| ArchEFIx86[EFI IA32]
    IdentifyArch -->|10| ArchEFIBC[EFI BC]
    IdentifyArch -->|11| ArchARM64[ARM 64-bit UEFI]
    IdentifyArch -->|Other| ArchOther[Other Architecture]
    
    ArchX86 --> ExtractUUID[Extract PXE UUID<br/>Option 97 if Present]
    ArchX64Legacy --> ExtractUUID
    ArchEFIx64 --> ExtractUUID
    ArchEFIx86 --> ExtractUUID
    ArchEFIBC --> ExtractUUID
    ArchARM64 --> ExtractUUID
    ArchOther --> ExtractUUID
    
    ExtractUUID --> CheckProxyMode{Proxy DHCP<br/>Mode?}
    CheckProxyMode -->|Yes| ProxyMode[Proxy Mode Processing<br/>No IP Allocation]
    CheckProxyMode -->|No| StandardAlloc[Standard IP Allocation]
    
    ProxyMode --> SelectBootFile[Select Boot File<br/>Based on Architecture]
    StandardAlloc --> SelectBootFile
    
    SelectBootFile --> CheckTagMatch{Tag-Based<br/>Boot Config?}
    CheckTagMatch -->|Yes| TagSelect["dhcp-boot=tag:arch,file"]
    CheckTagMatch -->|No| DefaultSelect[Default dhcp-boot]
    
    TagSelect --> SetBootFile[Set Boot Filename<br/>Option 67]
    DefaultSelect --> SetBootFile
    
    SetBootFile --> SetTFTPServer[Set TFTP Server<br/>Option 66 sname Field]
    SetTFTPServer --> CheckMenuConfig{PXE Menu<br/>Configured?}
    
    CheckMenuConfig -->|No| SendOffer[Send DHCPOFFER<br/>with Boot Parameters]
    CheckMenuConfig -->|Yes| AddMenuOpts[Add PXE Menu Options]
    
    AddMenuOpts --> SetPrompt["pxe-prompt:<br/>Timeout, Message Text"]
    SetPrompt --> AddServices[Add pxe-service Entries<br/>Menu Items by Architecture]
    AddServices --> SetDiscCtrl[Set Discovery Control<br/>Option 6]
    SetDiscCtrl --> SendOffer
    
    SendOffer --> ClientRecvOffer[Client Receives OFFER]
    ClientRecvOffer --> CheckMenu{Menu<br/>Present?}
    
    CheckMenu -->|No| DirectBoot[Direct Boot<br/>Use Specified File]
    CheckMenu -->|Yes| DisplayMenu[Display Boot Menu<br/>to User]
    
    DisplayMenu --> UserSelect[User Selects Option<br/>or Timeout Default]
    UserSelect --> SendBootReq[Client Sends<br/>PXE Boot Server Request]
    
    SendBootReq --> ServerRecvBootReq[Server Receives<br/>Boot Server Request]
    ServerRecvBootReq --> SelectSpecific[Select Specific<br/>Boot File for Choice]
    SelectSpecific --> SendBootResp[Send Boot Server<br/>Response with File]
    
    SendBootResp --> TFTPRequest[Client Initiates<br/>TFTP Transfer]
    DirectBoot --> TFTPRequest
    
    StandardDHCP --> End([Non-PXE DHCP])
    TFTPRequest --> TFTPFlow[TFTP Transfer Workflow<br/>See Section 4.6.2]
    
    style CheckVendor fill:#e1f5ff
    style IdentifyArch fill:#fff4e1
    style DisplayMenu fill:#e1ffe1
```

#### 4.6.1.2 Architecture-Specific Boot Files

Dnsmasq supports architecture-specific boot file selection through tag-based configuration matching client architecture option 93:

| Architecture Code | Architecture Name | Typical Boot File | Tag Example |
|------------------|-------------------|-------------------|-------------|
| 0 | Intel x86 BIOS | `pxelinux.0` | `tag:x86` |
| 6 | x86-64 Legacy BIOS | `pxelinux.0` | `tag:x64-legacy` |
| 7 | EFI x86-64 | `bootx64.efi` | `tag:efi-x64` |
| 9 | EFI IA32 | `bootia32.efi` | `tag:efi-ia32` |
| 11 | ARM 64-bit UEFI | `grubaa64.efi` | `tag:arm64-efi` |

Configuration example demonstrating architecture-specific selection:
```
# Tag matching for architecture detection
dhcp-match=set:x86,option:client-arch,0
dhcp-match=set:efi-x64,option:client-arch,7
dhcp-match=set:efi-ia32,option:client-arch,9

#### Architecture-specific boot files
dhcp-boot=tag:x86,pxelinux.0
dhcp-boot=tag:efi-x64,bootx64.efi
dhcp-boot=tag:efi-ia32,bootia32.efi
```

### 4.6.2 TFTP File Transfer Workflow

The TFTP (Trivial File Transfer Protocol) server provides read-only file transfer services primarily for network boot scenarios, implementing RFC 1350 with blocksize negotiation extensions.

#### 4.6.2.1 TFTP Transfer Lifecycle

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    ClientReq[PXE Client Sends<br/>TFTP Read Request<br/>RRQ Packet] --> ServerRecv[TFTP Server Receives<br/>on UDP Port 69]
    
    ServerRecv --> ParseReq[Parse RRQ<br/>Extract Filename<br/>Extract Mode]
    
    ParseReq --> CheckRoot{File Path<br/>Within tftp-root?}
    CheckRoot -->|No| SendError[Send TFTP ERROR<br/>Access Violation]
    CheckRoot -->|Yes| CheckSecure{tftp-secure<br/>Mode?}
    
    CheckSecure -->|Yes| CheckPerm[Verify File Permissions<br/>World-Readable Required]
    CheckSecure -->|No| OpenFile[Open File<br/>for Reading]
    
    CheckPerm -->|Fail| SendError
    CheckPerm -->|Pass| OpenFile
    
    OpenFile --> CheckExists{File<br/>Exists?}
    CheckExists -->|No| SendNotFound[Send TFTP ERROR<br/>File Not Found]
    CheckExists -->|Yes| ParseOpts[Parse TFTP Options<br/>blksize, tsize, timeout]
    
    ParseOpts --> NegotiateBlock{Blocksize<br/>Negotiation?}
    NegotiateBlock -->|Yes| SendOACK[Send OACK<br/>Option Acknowledgment]
    NegotiateBlock -->|No| UseDefault[Use Default 512 Bytes]
    
    SendOACK --> WaitACK{Wait for<br/>ACK of OACK}
    UseDefault --> ReadBlock[Read First Block<br/>from File]
    
    WaitACK -->|Timeout| ResendOACK[Resend OACK<br/>Max 3 Retries]
    WaitACK -->|ACK Received| ReadBlock
    ResendOACK --> CheckRetries{Retries<br/>Exhausted?}
    CheckRetries -->|Yes| CloseAbort[Close File<br/>Abort Transfer]
    CheckRetries -->|No| WaitACK
    
    ReadBlock --> BuildData[Build DATA Packet<br/>Block Number<br/>Data Bytes]
    
    BuildData --> SendData[Send DATA Packet<br/>to Client]
    SendData --> StartTimer[Start Timeout Timer<br/>Default 5 seconds]
    
    StartTimer --> WaitACKData{Wait for<br/>ACK}
    
    WaitACKData -->|Timeout| ResendData[Resend DATA Packet<br/>Max 3 Retries]
    WaitACKData -->|Wrong Block ACK| IgnoreACK[Ignore ACK<br/>Continue Waiting]
    WaitACKData -->|Correct ACK| CheckLastBlock{Last Block<br/>Sent?}
    
    ResendData --> CheckRetries
    IgnoreACK --> WaitACKData
    
    CheckLastBlock -->|No, More Data| IncrBlock[Increment Block Number]
    CheckLastBlock -->|Yes, EOF| TransferComplete[Transfer Complete]
    
    IncrBlock --> ReadBlock
    
    TransferComplete --> CloseFile[Close File]
    CloseFile --> FreeConn[Free Connection Slot<br/>Max 50 Concurrent]
    
    FreeConn --> CheckScript{TFTP Logging<br/>Script Enabled?}
    CheckScript -->|Yes| ExecScript[queue_script<br/>ACTION=tftp<br/>Filename, Client IP]
    CheckScript -->|No| LogComplete[Log Transfer Complete]
    
    ExecScript --> LogComplete
    LogComplete --> Complete([TFTP Transfer Done])
    
    SendError --> Complete
    SendNotFound --> Complete
    CloseAbort --> Complete
    
    style CheckRoot fill:#fff4e1
    style CheckExists fill:#ffe1e1
    style WaitACKData fill:#e1f5ff
    style CheckLastBlock fill:#fff4e1
```

#### 4.6.2.2 TFTP Security and Resource Management

**Security Features**:

- **Root Directory Restriction**: All file paths validated to remain within configured `tftp-root` directory, preventing directory traversal attacks
- **Secure Mode** (`tftp-secure`): When enabled, only world-readable files are accessible, preventing unauthorized access to sensitive files
- **Lowercase Filename Conversion** (`tftp-lowercase`): Normalizes filenames to lowercase for case-insensitive filesystem compatibility

**Resource Limits**:

- **Concurrent Connection Limit**: Maximum 50 concurrent TFTP transfers (`TFTP_MAX_CONNECTIONS` in `src/config.h`)
- **Connection Timeout**: Default 5-second timeout for each block acknowledgment
- **Retry Limit**: Maximum 3 retries per packet before aborting transfer
- **Blocksize Negotiation**: Configurable block size from 512 bytes (default) to 1468 bytes (maximum Ethernet MTU-safe)

**Connection Management**:

When the concurrent connection limit is reached, new TFTP requests are rejected with a TFTP ERROR code indicating resource unavailability. This prevents memory exhaustion attacks where malicious clients initiate excessive transfers. Completed or timed-out transfers immediately free their connection slots for reuse.

## 4.7 Script Execution and Integration Workflows

### 4.7.1 Helper Process Architecture

Dnsmasq implements privilege-separated script execution through a dedicated helper process that retains root privileges for external script invocation while the main daemon operates with reduced privileges.

#### 4.7.1.1 Helper Process Initialization and Communication

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    DaemonStart[Daemon Startup<br/>Running as Root] --> CreatePipe[create_helper<br/>Create IPC Pipe<br/>Before Privilege Drop]
    
    CreatePipe --> ForkHelper[fork Helper Process]
    ForkHelper --> SplitProc{Process Split}
    
    SplitProc -->|Parent: Main Daemon| DropPriv[Drop to Unprivileged User<br/>Close Write End of Pipe]
    SplitProc -->|Child: Helper| RetainRoot[Retain Root Privileges<br/>Close Read End of Pipe]
    
    DropPriv --> MainLoop[Main Event Loop<br/>Reduced Privileges]
    RetainRoot --> LoadLua{Lua Script<br/>Configured?}
    
    LoadLua -->|Yes| InitLua[Initialize Lua VM<br/>Load Script File<br/>Call init Function]
    LoadLua -->|No| WaitEvents[Wait for Events<br/>from Pipe]
    
    InitLua --> WaitEvents
    
    MainLoop --> LeaseEvent[DHCP Lease Event<br/>add, old, del]
    LeaseEvent --> BuildData[Build script_data Structure<br/>action, hwaddr, IP<br/>hostname, domain, client-id<br/>lease_expires, interface]
    
    BuildData --> WritePipe[Write to Pipe<br/>script_data Structure<br/>Variable-length Data]
    WritePipe --> Continue[Continue Main Loop]
    
    WaitEvents --> ReadPipe[read Blocks on Pipe]
    ReadPipe --> DataRecv[Data Received]
    DataRecv --> ParseAction[Parse Action Type]
    
    ParseAction --> CheckAction{Action Type?}
    CheckAction -->|ACTION_ADD| SetEnvAdd[Set Environment<br/>ACTION=add]
    CheckAction -->|ACTION_DEL| SetEnvDel[Set Environment<br/>ACTION=del]
    CheckAction -->|ACTION_OLD| SetEnvOld[Set Environment<br/>ACTION=old]
    CheckAction -->|ACTION_TFTP| SetEnvTFTP[Set Environment<br/>ACTION=tftp]
    CheckAction -->|ACTION_ARP| SetEnvARP[Set Environment<br/>ACTION=arp]
    
    SetEnvAdd --> SetCommonEnv[Set Common Environment<br/>DNSMASQ_MAC_ADDRESS<br/>DNSMASQ_IP_ADDRESS<br/>DNSMASQ_HOSTNAME<br/>DNSMASQ_DOMAIN<br/>DNSMASQ_INTERFACE<br/>DNSMASQ_CLIENT_ID]
    SetEnvDel --> SetCommonEnv
    SetEnvOld --> SetCommonEnv
    SetEnvTFTP --> SetCommonEnv
    SetEnvARP --> SetCommonEnv
    
    SetCommonEnv --> CheckDHCP6{DHCPv6<br/>Event?}
    CheckDHCP6 -->|Yes| SetDHCP6Env[Set DHCPv6 Environment<br/>DNSMASQ_IAID<br/>DNSMASQ_SERVER_DUID]
    CheckDHCP6 -->|No| CheckTags{Tags<br/>Present?}
    
    SetDHCP6Env --> CheckTags
    CheckTags -->|Yes| SetTagsEnv[Set DNSMASQ_TAGS]
    CheckTags -->|No| CheckMode{Execution<br/>Mode?}
    
    SetTagsEnv --> CheckMode
    CheckMode -->|External Script| ForkExec[fork Child Process]
    CheckMode -->|Lua Script| CallLua[Call Lua lease Function]
    
    ForkExec --> ExecScript[exec External Script<br/>with Environment]
    ExecScript --> WaitChild[wait for Child<br/>Completion]
    WaitChild --> CheckStatus{Exit Status<br/>Success?}
    CheckStatus -->|Error| LogError[Log Script Error]
    CheckStatus -->|Success| LogSuccess[Log Script Success]
    
    CallLua --> PushTable[Push Environment Table<br/>to Lua Stack]
    PushTable --> CallFunction[Call lease Function<br/>Pass action, address, hostname]
    CallFunction --> CheckReturn{Return<br/>Value?}
    CheckReturn -->|Error| LogError
    CheckReturn -->|Success| LogSuccess
    
    LogError --> WaitEvents
    LogSuccess --> WaitEvents
    Continue --> LeaseEvent
    
    style SplitProc fill:#e1f5ff
    style CheckAction fill:#fff4e1
    style CheckMode fill:#fff4e1
```

#### 4.7.1.2 Event Types and Environment Variables

**Lease Event Types**:

- **ACTION_ADD**: New DHCP lease created or renewed
- **ACTION_DEL**: DHCP lease released or expired
- **ACTION_OLD**: Existing lease (triggered during configuration reload via SIGHUP)
- **ACTION_OLD_HOSTNAME**: Hostname changed for existing lease
- **ACTION_TFTP**: TFTP file transfer completed
- **ACTION_ARP**: ARP cache entry added
- **ACTION_ARP_DEL**: ARP cache entry removed
- **ACTION_RELAY_SNOOP**: DHCPv6 relay snooping event

**Environment Variables Passed to Scripts**:

| Variable Name | Description | Example Value |
|---------------|-------------|---------------|
| `DNSMASQ_LEASE_ACTION` | Action type | `add`, `del`, `old` |
| `DNSMASQ_MAC_ADDRESS` | Client MAC address | `00:11:22:33:44:55` |
| `DNSMASQ_IP_ADDRESS` | Assigned IP address | `192.168.1.100` or IPv6 |
| `DNSMASQ_HOSTNAME` | Client hostname | `workstation-42` |
| `DNSMASQ_DOMAIN` | Domain suffix | `example.com` |
| `DNSMASQ_INTERFACE` | Interface name | `eth0`, `br0` |
| `DNSMASQ_CLIENT_ID` | DHCP client identifier | Hex string or text |
| `DNSMASQ_LEASE_EXPIRES` | Lease expiration timestamp | Unix timestamp |
| `DNSMASQ_IAID` | DHCPv6 Identity Association ID | Numeric value |
| `DNSMASQ_SERVER_DUID` | DHCPv6 Server DUID | Hex string |
| `DNSMASQ_TAGS` | Matched configuration tags | Comma-separated list |
| `DNSMASQ_TFTP_FILE` | TFTP filename transferred | `pxelinux.0` |
| `DNSMASQ_TFTP_SIZE` | File size in bytes | Numeric value |

### 4.7.2 External Script Integration Use Cases

#### 4.7.2.1 Dynamic Firewall Rule Management

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    LeaseAdd[DHCP Lease Created<br/>ACTION=add] --> ScriptExec[Execute Script with<br/>IP, MAC, Hostname]
    
    ScriptExec --> CheckPolicy{Device<br/>Known?}
    CheckPolicy -->|Unknown| GuestVLAN[Add Firewall Rule<br/>Restrict to Guest VLAN]
    CheckPolicy -->|Known| CheckType{Device<br/>Type?}
    
    CheckType -->|Trusted| AllowAll[Add Firewall Rule<br/>Full Network Access]
    CheckType -->|IoT| IsolateIoT[Add Firewall Rule<br/>Internet Only, Isolated]
    CheckType -->|Guest| GuestVLAN
    
    GuestVLAN --> LogRule[Log Rule Addition]
    AllowAll --> LogRule
    IsolateIoT --> LogRule
    
    LogRule --> Complete([Script Complete])
    
    LeaseRelease[DHCP Lease Released<br/>ACTION=del] --> RemoveScript[Execute Script<br/>IP, MAC]
    RemoveScript --> FindRule[Find Firewall Rules<br/>Matching IP or MAC]
    FindRule --> DeleteRules[Delete Rules<br/>via iptables/nftables]
    DeleteRules --> LogRemoval[Log Rule Removal]
    LogRemoval --> Complete
    
    style CheckPolicy fill:#fff4e1
    style CheckType fill:#e1f5ff
```

#### 4.7.2.2 Dynamic DNS Update Integration

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    LeaseAdd[DHCP Lease Created<br/>with Hostname] --> ScriptExec[Execute DDNS Script]
    
    ScriptExec --> CheckDDNS{DDNS<br/>Configured?}
    CheckDDNS -->|No| SkipDDNS[Skip Update]
    CheckDDNS -->|Yes| BuildUpdate[Build DNS UPDATE Packet<br/>RFC 2136]
    
    BuildUpdate --> CheckAuth{Authentication<br/>Required?}
    CheckAuth -->|Yes| SignUpdate[Sign with TSIG Key<br/>RFC 2845]
    CheckAuth -->|No| SendUpdate[Send DNS UPDATE<br/>to Authoritative Server]
    
    SignUpdate --> SendUpdate
    SendUpdate --> WaitResponse{Response<br/>Received?}
    
    WaitResponse -->|Timeout| RetryUpdate[Retry Update<br/>Max 3 Attempts]
    WaitResponse -->|NOERROR| LogSuccess[Log: DDNS Update Success]
    WaitResponse -->|Error| LogError[Log: DDNS Update Failed]
    
    RetryUpdate --> CheckRetries{Retries<br/>Exhausted?}
    CheckRetries -->|Yes| LogError
    CheckRetries -->|No| SendUpdate
    
    LogSuccess --> Complete([Script Complete])
    LogError --> Complete
    SkipDDNS --> Complete
    
    style CheckDDNS fill:#fff4e1
    style WaitResponse fill:#e1f5ff
```

## 4.8 Configuration Reload Workflow

### 4.8.1 SIGHUP-Triggered Reconfiguration

The configuration reload workflow enables dynamic reconfiguration without daemon restart, preserving active connections and lease state while applying new configuration parameters.

#### 4.8.1.1 Complete Reload Sequence

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    SendSIGHUP[Administrator Sends<br/>kill -HUP $PID] --> SigHandler[sig_handler Receives<br/>SIGHUP]
    
    SigHandler --> WriteEvent[Write EVENT_RELOAD<br/>to Signal Pipe]
    WriteEvent --> EventQueue[Event Queued]
    
    EventQueue --> EventLoop[Main Event Loop<br/>Detects Pipe Readable]
    EventLoop --> AsyncEvent[async_event<br/>Reads EVENT_RELOAD]
    
    AsyncEvent --> IncrSOA[Increment SOA Serial<br/>for Auth Zones]
    IncrSOA --> ClearCache[clear_cache_and_reload]
    
    ClearCache --> PreserveDHCP[Preserve F_DHCP Entries<br/>Keep DHCP Hostnames]
    PreserveDHCP --> PreserveHosts[Preserve F_HOSTS Entries<br/>Keep Static Hosts]
    PreserveHosts --> FlushUpstream[Flush F_UPSTREAM Entries<br/>Clear Cached DNS]
    
    FlushUpstream --> ReloadConfig[Read Configuration File<br/>Parse All Directives]
    ReloadConfig --> CheckSyntax{Configuration<br/>Valid?}
    
    CheckSyntax -->|Error| LogError[Log Configuration Error]
    CheckSyntax -->|Valid| ProcessIncludes[Process conf-dir<br/>Include Files]
    
    LogError --> RevertConfig[Keep Previous Config<br/>Continue Operation]
    ProcessIncludes --> ApplySettings[Apply New Settings]
    
    ApplySettings --> ReloadResolv{Monitor<br/>resolv.conf?}
    ReloadResolv -->|Yes| ReadResolv[Re-read /etc/resolv.conf]
    ReloadResolv -->|No| ReloadUpstream[reload_servers]
    
    ReadResolv --> ParseUpstream[Parse Upstream Servers]
    ParseUpstream --> ReloadUpstream
    
    ReloadUpstream --> UpdateServerList[Update Upstream Server List]
    UpdateServerList --> CheckReach[Check Server Reachability]
    CheckReach --> UpdatePriority[Update Server Priorities]
    
    UpdatePriority --> ReloadHosts[Re-read /etc/hosts]
    ReloadHosts --> ReloadAddn[Re-read addn-hosts Files]
    ReloadAddn --> UpdateCache[Update Cache with<br/>New Static Entries]
    
    UpdateCache --> RemoveObsolete[Remove Obsolete<br/>Static Entries]
    RemoveObsolete --> RerunScripts[rerun_scripts]
    
    RerunScripts --> IterLeases[Iterate All Active Leases]
    IterLeases --> CheckMoreLeases{More<br/>Leases?}
    
    CheckMoreLeases -->|Yes| ExecOld[queue_script<br/>ACTION=old<br/>Sync External State]
    CheckMoreLeases -->|No| EnumInterfaces[enumerate_interfaces]
    
    ExecOld --> NextLease[Next Lease]
    NextLease --> CheckMoreLeases
    
    EnumInterfaces --> CheckNewIF{New<br/>Interfaces?}
    CheckNewIF -->|Yes| CreateListeners[Create New Listener Sockets]
    CheckNewIF -->|No| CheckRemovedIF{Interfaces<br/>Removed?}
    
    CreateListeners --> CheckRemovedIF
    CheckRemovedIF -->|Yes| CloseListeners[Close Obsolete Sockets]
    CheckRemovedIF -->|No| UpdateRoutes[Update Routing Tables]
    
    CloseListeners --> UpdateRoutes
    UpdateRoutes --> LogReload[Log: Configuration Reloaded]
    LogReload --> Complete([Reload Complete<br/>Resume Normal Operation])
    
    RevertConfig --> LogRevert[Log: Using Previous Config]
    LogRevert --> Complete
    
    style CheckSyntax fill:#fff4e1
    style LogError fill:#ffe1e1
    style CheckMoreLeases fill:#e1f5ff
```

#### 4.8.1.2 Inotify-Based Automatic Reload

On Linux systems with inotify support, dnsmasq automatically monitors configuration files for changes and triggers reload without manual SIGHUP delivery.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    DaemonStart[Daemon Startup] --> CheckInotify{Inotify<br/>Support?}
    CheckInotify -->|No| NoMonitor[Manual SIGHUP Only]
    CheckInotify -->|Yes| InitInotify[Initialize Inotify FD]
    
    InitInotify --> WatchResolv{Monitor<br/>resolv.conf?}
    WatchResolv -->|Yes| AddResolvWatch[inotify_add_watch<br/>/etc/resolv.conf<br/>IN_MODIFY, IN_CLOSE_WRITE]
    WatchResolv -->|No| WatchHostsDir{Monitor<br/>dhcp-hostsdir?}
    
    AddResolvWatch --> WatchHostsDir
    WatchHostsDir -->|Yes| AddHostsWatch[inotify_add_watch<br/>dhcp-hostsdir<br/>IN_MODIFY, IN_CREATE]
    WatchHostsDir -->|No| MonitorLoop[Add Inotify FD<br/>to Event Loop]
    
    AddHostsWatch --> MonitorLoop
    MonitorLoop --> EventPoll[poll Monitors<br/>Inotify FD]
    
    EventPoll --> FileChange{File<br/>Changed?}
    FileChange -->|No| EventPoll
    FileChange -->|Yes| ReadEvent[Read Inotify Event]
    
    ReadEvent --> CheckEvent{Event<br/>Type?}
    CheckEvent -->|resolv.conf Modified| TriggerResolv[Trigger Upstream<br/>Server Reload]
    CheckEvent -->|hostsdir Modified| TriggerHosts[Trigger Hosts<br/>File Reload]
    
    TriggerResolv --> SynthSIGHUP[Synthesize EVENT_RELOAD]
    TriggerHosts --> SynthSIGHUP
    SynthSIGHUP --> ReloadSeq[Execute Reload Sequence<br/>See Section 4.8.1.1]
    
    ReloadSeq --> EventPoll
    NoMonitor --> ManualOnly([Manual Reload Only])
    
    style CheckInotify fill:#e1f5ff
    style FileChange fill:#fff4e1
```

### 4.8.2 Reload Impact on Active Operations

**DNS Query Preservation**: Active DNS queries in flight (forward records with pending upstream responses) are not affected by reload. These queries complete normally using the configuration active when they were initiated. New queries after reload use updated configuration.

**DHCP Lease Continuity**: All active DHCP leases are preserved in the lease database and remain valid across reload. The lease database file is re-read to capture any external modifications, but existing leases in memory are not discarded.

**TCP Connection Handling**: Active TCP connections (DNS over TCP, TFTP transfers) continue operating with their original configuration until completion. New TCP connections use updated configuration.

**Cache Coherency**: The cache clearing operation removes all F_UPSTREAM entries (upstream DNS responses) but preserves F_HOSTS (static host file entries) and F_DHCP (DHCP lease hostnames). This ensures locally configured names remain resolvable immediately after reload without requiring re-population.

**Script Notification**: The `rerun_scripts()` function executes lease scripts with `ACTION=old` for all active leases, allowing external systems to synchronize state with the reloaded configuration. This is particularly important for firewall rule management and dynamic DNS systems that maintain state synchronized with DHCP leases.

## 4.9 Error Handling and Recovery Workflows

### 4.9.1 DNS Error Handling

#### 4.9.1.1 Upstream Server Failure Recovery

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    SendQuery[Send DNS Query<br/>to Upstream Server] --> StartTimeout[Start Timeout Timer<br/>Default 10 seconds]
    
    StartTimeout --> WaitResponse{Wait for<br/>Response}
    WaitResponse -->|Response Received| ProcessResp[Process Response]
    WaitResponse -->|Timeout| IncrFail[Increment Server<br/>Failure Count]
    
    IncrFail --> CheckAlt{Alternative<br/>Servers Available?}
    CheckAlt -->|Yes| SelectAlt[Select Next Upstream<br/>Prefer Low Failure Count]
    CheckAlt -->|No| AllFailed[All Upstreams Failed]
    
    SelectAlt --> RetryQuery[Retry Query with<br/>Alternative Server]
    RetryQuery --> StartTimeout
    
    AllFailed --> CheckCache{Stale Cache<br/>Entry Available?}
    CheckCache -->|Yes| ServeStale[Serve Stale Entry<br/>with Reduced TTL]
    CheckCache -->|No| ReturnSERVFAIL[Return SERVFAIL<br/>to Client]
    
    ProcessResp --> CheckRCODE{Response<br/>RCODE?}
    CheckRCODE -->|NOERROR| DecrFail[Decrement Server<br/>Failure Count]
    CheckRCODE -->|SERVFAIL| CheckOther{Other<br/>Servers?}
    CheckRCODE -->|NXDOMAIN| CacheNegative[Negative Cache<br/>NXDOMAIN]
    
    CheckOther -->|Yes| SelectAlt
    CheckOther -->|No| PassSERVFAIL[Pass SERVFAIL<br/>to Client]
    
    DecrFail --> ReturnResponse[Return Response<br/>to Client]
    ServeStale --> LogStale[Log: Serving Stale Entry]
    ReturnSERVFAIL --> LogFail[Log: All Servers Failed]
    CacheNegative --> ReturnResponse
    
    LogStale --> Complete([Query Complete])
    ReturnResponse --> Complete
    ReturnSERVFAIL --> Complete
    PassSERVFAIL --> Complete
    LogFail --> Complete
    
    style CheckAlt fill:#fff4e1
    style AllFailed fill:#ffe1e1
    style CheckCache fill:#e1f5ff
```

#### 4.9.1.2 TCP Retry for Truncated Responses

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    RecvUDP[Receive UDP Response] --> CheckTC{TC Bit<br/>Set?}
    
    CheckTC -->|No| ProcessUDP[Process UDP Response]
    CheckTC -->|Yes| CheckSize{Response<br/>Size Known?}
    
    CheckSize -->|EDNS0 Size| CheckEDNS{Size Exceeds<br/>Client EDNS0?}
    CheckSize -->|Unknown| RetryTCP[Retry Query over TCP]
    
    CheckEDNS -->|Yes| RetryTCP
    CheckEDNS -->|No| ProcessUDP
    
    RetryTCP --> CreateTCP[Create TCP Connection<br/>to Upstream]
    CreateTCP --> ConnResult{Connection<br/>Result?}
    
    ConnResult -->|Failed| ConnError[Log Connection Error]
    ConnResult -->|Success| SendTCPQuery[Send Query over TCP]
    
    SendTCPQuery --> SetTCPTimeout[Set TCP Timeout<br/>5 seconds]
    SetTCPTimeout --> WaitTCPResp{Wait for<br/>TCP Response}
    
    WaitTCPResp -->|Timeout| CloseTCP[Close TCP Connection]
    WaitTCPResp -->|Response| RecvTCPResp[Receive Complete Response]
    
    RecvTCPResp --> CheckTCPSize{Response<br/>Complete?}
    CheckTCPSize -->|Partial| ContinueRead[Continue Reading]
    CheckTCPSize -->|Complete| ProcessTCP[Process TCP Response]
    
    ContinueRead --> WaitTCPResp
    ProcessTCP --> CloseTCPConn[Close TCP Connection]
    CloseTCPConn --> ReturnResponse[Return to Client]
    
    CloseTCP --> RetryError[Return Error to Client]
    ConnError --> RetryError
    
    ProcessUDP --> CompleteUDP([UDP Query Complete])
    ReturnResponse --> CompleteTCP([TCP Query Complete])
    RetryError --> CompleteTCP
    
    style CheckTC fill:#fff4e1
    style ConnResult fill:#ffe1e1
    style CheckTCPSize fill:#e1f5ff
```

### 4.9.2 DHCP Error Handling

#### 4.9.2.1 Address Pool Exhaustion

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    RecvDiscover[Receive DHCPDISCOVER] --> AllocAddr[address_allocate<br/>Find Free Address]
    
    AllocAddr --> CheckPool{Address<br/>Available?}
    CheckPool -->|Yes| AssignAddr[Assign Address<br/>Send DHCPOFFER]
    CheckPool -->|No| CountLeases[Count Active Leases]
    
    CountLeases --> CheckExpired{Expired<br/>Leases Exist?}
    CheckExpired -->|Yes| PruneExpired[Prune Expired Leases<br/>Free Addresses]
    CheckExpired -->|No| CheckConflict{Declined<br/>Addresses Exist?}
    
    PruneExpired --> RetryAlloc[Retry Allocation]
    RetryAlloc --> CheckRetry{Address<br/>Now Available?}
    CheckRetry -->|Yes| AssignAddr
    CheckRetry -->|No| CheckConflict
    
    CheckConflict -->|Yes, Expired Backoff| FreeDeclined[Free Declined Addresses<br/>After 24 Hour Backoff]
    CheckConflict -->|No| LogExhaustion[Log: Address Pool<br/>Exhausted]
    
    FreeDeclined --> RetryAlloc
    LogExhaustion --> DropDiscover[Drop DHCPDISCOVER<br/>No Response Sent]
    
    DropDiscover --> NotifyAdmin[Notify Administrator<br/>via Syslog Priority WARN]
    NotifyAdmin --> SuggestExpansion[Log: Consider Expanding<br/>dhcp-range Pool]
    
    RecvRequest[Receive DHCPREQUEST<br/>for Unavailable IP] --> CheckReqIP{Requested IP<br/>in Pool?}
    
    CheckReqIP -->|No| SendNAK[Send DHCPNAK]
    CheckReqIP -->|Yes, In Use| CheckOwner{Same<br/>Client?}
    
    CheckOwner -->|Yes| RenewLease[Renew Lease<br/>Send DHCPACK]
    CheckOwner -->|No| SendNAK
    
    SendNAK --> ClientRetry[Client Returns to<br/>INIT State]
    ClientRetry --> NewDiscover[Send New DHCPDISCOVER]
    
    AssignAddr --> NormalFlow([Normal DHCP Flow])
    RenewLease --> NormalFlow
    NewDiscover --> RecvDiscover
    SuggestExpansion --> End([Exhaustion Handled])
    
    style CheckPool fill:#ffe1e1
    style LogExhaustion fill:#ffe1e1
    style CheckExpired fill:#fff4e1
```

#### 4.9.2.2 IP Address Conflict Detection and Resolution

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    BeforeOffer[Before Sending DHCPOFFER] --> CheckPingEnabled{ICMP Ping<br/>Check Enabled?}
    
    CheckPingEnabled -->|No| SendOffer[Send DHCPOFFER<br/>Without Ping]
    CheckPingEnabled -->|Yes| SendICMP[Send ICMP Echo Request<br/>to Candidate IP]
    
    SendICMP --> StartWait[Wait for Response<br/>Timeout 1 second]
    StartWait --> CheckReply{ICMP Echo<br/>Reply Received?}
    
    CheckReply -->|No, Available| SendOffer
    CheckReply -->|Yes, Conflict| LogConflict[Log: IP Address Conflict<br/>Detected via Ping]
    
    LogConflict --> MarkInUse[Mark Address<br/>as In Use]
    MarkInUse --> TryNext[Try Next Available<br/>Address from Pool]
    
    TryNext --> CheckMore{More<br/>Addresses?}
    CheckMore -->|Yes| SendICMP
    CheckMore -->|No| ExhaustPool[Pool Exhausted<br/>Drop DHCPDISCOVER]
    
    ClientDecline[Client Sends DHCPDECLINE<br/>After Detecting Conflict] --> RecvDecline[Server Receives DECLINE]
    
    RecvDecline --> ExtractIP[Extract requested-ip<br/>from DECLINE]
    ExtractIP --> ValidateDecline{Valid<br/>DECLINE?}
    
    ValidateDecline -->|No| IgnoreDecline[Ignore Invalid DECLINE]
    ValidateDecline -->|Yes| CheckStatic{Static<br/>Reservation?}
    
    CheckStatic -->|Yes| DisableStatic[Disable Static Address<br/>for 24 Hours]
    CheckStatic -->|No| MarkDeclined[Mark Address as<br/>DECLINED]
    
    DisableStatic --> SetBackoff[Set DECLINE_BACKOFF<br/>24 Hour Timer]
    MarkDeclined --> SetBackoff
    
    SetBackoff --> ForceDifferent[Force Client to Use<br/>Different IP Next Request]
    ForceDifferent --> LogDecline[Log: Address Declined<br/>by Client MAC]
    
    LogDecline --> InvestigateConflict[Administrator: Investigate<br/>Duplicate IP Usage]
    
    SendOffer --> NormalFlow([Normal DHCP Flow])
    ExhaustPool --> ErrorFlow([Address Exhaustion])
    IgnoreDecline --> End([DECLINE Ignored])
    InvestigateConflict --> End
    
    style CheckReply fill:#ffe1e1
    style LogConflict fill:#ffe1e1
    style ValidateDecline fill:#fff4e1
```

### 4.9.3 DNSSEC Validation Failures

#### 4.9.3.1 DNSSEC Error Response Flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    ValidateResp[DNSSEC Validation<br/>in Progress] --> CheckResult{Validation<br/>Result?}
    
    CheckResult -->|SECURE| SetAD[Set AD Bit<br/>Return Response]
    CheckResult -->|INSECURE| NoAD[Clear AD Bit<br/>Return Response]
    CheckResult -->|BOGUS| CheckCD{Client Set<br/>CD Bit?}
    CheckResult -->|ABANDONED| LogAbandoned[Log: Validation Abandoned<br/>Resource Limits]
    
    CheckCD -->|Yes| ReturnBogus[Return Response<br/>with CD Bit<br/>Client Handles Validation]
    CheckCD -->|No| ReturnSERVFAIL[Return SERVFAIL<br/>Protect Client]
    
    LogAbandoned --> CheckCDAband{Client Set<br/>CD Bit?}
    CheckCDAband -->|Yes| ReturnBogus
    CheckCDAband -->|No| ReturnSERVFAIL
    
    ReturnSERVFAIL --> LogBogus[Log: DNSSEC BOGUS<br/>Domain Name<br/>Validation Failure Reason]
    
    LogBogus --> CheckEDE{Extended DNS<br/>Errors Enabled?}
    CheckEDE -->|Yes| AddEDE[Add EDE Option<br/>RFC 8914<br/>Specific Error Code]
    CheckEDE -->|No| SendSERVFAIL[Send SERVFAIL Response]
    
    AddEDE --> MapError{Error<br/>Type?}
    MapError -->|Signature Expired| EDE_SigExpired[EDE: Signature Expired]
    MapError -->|Signature Invalid| EDE_SigInvalid[EDE: DNSSEC Bogus]
    MapError -->|Missing DNSKEY| EDE_NoKey[EDE: DNSKEY Missing]
    MapError -->|DS Mismatch| EDE_DSFail[EDE: DS Digest Mismatch]
    
    EDE_SigExpired --> SendEDESERVFAIL[Send SERVFAIL<br/>with EDE Option]
    EDE_SigInvalid --> SendEDESERVFAIL
    EDE_NoKey --> SendEDESERVFAIL
    EDE_DSFail --> SendEDESERVFAIL
    
    SendSERVFAIL --> ClientRecv[Client Receives SERVFAIL]
    SendEDESERVFAIL --> ClientRecv
    
    ClientRecv --> ClientAction{Client<br/>Action?}
    ClientAction -->|Retry| RetryQuery[Client Retries Query<br/>May Use Different Server]
    ClientAction -->|Accept| AcceptFail[Client Accepts Failure<br/>DNS Resolution Failed]
    
    SetAD --> SecureResp([Secure Response])
    NoAD --> InsecureResp([Insecure Response])
    ReturnBogus --> BogusResp([Bogus Response to Client])
    RetryQuery --> End([Query Retry])
    AcceptFail --> End
    
    style CheckResult fill:#fff4e1
    style ReturnSERVFAIL fill:#ffe1e1
    style LogBogus fill:#ffe1e1
```

### 4.9.4 Resource Limit Enforcement

#### 4.9.4.1 Query Rate Limiting and Forward Record Exhaustion

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    RecvQuery[Receive DNS Query] --> GetForward[get_new_frec<br/>Allocate Forward Record]
    
    GetForward --> CheckAvail{Forward Record<br/>Available?}
    CheckAvail -->|Yes| AllocFREC[Allocate FREC<br/>Initialize State]
    CheckAvail -->|No| QueryFull[query_full<br/>Forward Records Exhausted]
    
    QueryFull --> PruneExpired[Prune Expired<br/>Forward Records]
    PruneExpired --> RetryAlloc{FREC<br/>Now Available?}
    
    RetryAlloc -->|Yes| AllocFREC
    RetryAlloc -->|No| CountActive[Count Active Queries]
    
    CountActive --> CheckLimit{Active Queries<br/>Exceed Limit?}
    CheckLimit -->|No| WaitSlot[Wait for Free Slot<br/>Queue Query]
    CheckLimit -->|Yes| ReturnREFUSED[Return REFUSED<br/>to Client]
    
    ReturnREFUSED --> LogRefused[Log: Query Refused<br/>Resource Exhaustion]
    LogRefused --> RateLimit[Rate Limiting Active<br/>Protect Server]
    
    WaitSlot --> CheckTimeout{Queue<br/>Timeout?}
    CheckTimeout -->|Expired| ReturnREFUSED
    CheckTimeout -->|Slot Available| AllocFREC
    
    AllocFREC --> ProcessQuery[Process DNS Query<br/>Normal Flow]
    
    ProcessQuery --> Complete([Query Processed])
    RateLimit --> ClientRetry[Client May Retry<br/>with Backoff]
    ClientRetry --> End([Resource Protection Active])
    
    style CheckAvail fill:#ffe1e1
    style CheckLimit fill:#ffe1e1
```

## 4.10 Process Flow Summary and SLA Considerations

### 4.10.1 Performance Characteristics

The following table summarizes typical performance characteristics and timing constraints for each major workflow under normal operating conditions:

| Workflow | Typical Latency | Timeout Value | SLA Target |
|----------|----------------|---------------|------------|
| **DNS Cache Hit** | <1 ms | N/A (immediate) | 99.9% <1ms |
| **DNS Cache Miss (UDP)** | Upstream + 5-10ms | 10 seconds | 95% <100ms |
| **DNS over TCP** | Upstream + 10-20ms | 5 seconds | 90% <200ms |
| **DNSSEC Validation** | Upstream + 20-100ms | 10 seconds per query | 90% <500ms |
| **DHCPv4 DISCOVER-ACK** | 5-20 ms | N/A (no timeout) | 99% <50ms |
| **DHCPv6 SOLICIT-REPLY** | 5-20 ms | N/A (no timeout) | 99% <50ms |
| **DHCP Lease Renewal** | 5-10 ms | N/A (no timeout) | 99.9% <20ms |
| **TFTP Block Transfer** | 10-50 ms per block | 5 seconds per block | 95% <100ms/block |
| **PXE Boot Complete** | 10-60 seconds | N/A (multi-step) | 90% <60s |
| **Configuration Reload** | 100-500 ms | N/A (synchronous) | 99% <1s |
| **External Script Execution** | 50-500 ms | Configurable | Depends on script |

### 4.10.2 Reliability and Fault Tolerance

**DNS Service Availability**:
- **Upstream Failure Tolerance**: Automatic failover to alternative upstream servers when primary fails
- **Stale Cache Serving**: Ability to serve slightly stale cached entries when all upstreams unavailable
- **Cache Preservation**: DHCP and hosts file entries never evicted, ensuring critical local names always resolvable

**DHCP Service Continuity**:
- **Lease Database Persistence**: All leases survive daemon restart through disk persistence
- **Graceful Degradation**: Continues serving existing leases even if pool exhausted for new assignments
- **Conflict Detection**: ICMP ping-based duplicate address detection prevents IP conflicts

**Error Recovery Mechanisms**:
- **Automatic Retry**: Failed upstream queries automatically retried with exponential backoff
- **TCP Fallback**: Truncated UDP responses automatically trigger TCP retry
- **Watchdog Timers**: All blocking operations protected by timeout mechanisms

# 5. System Architecture

## 5.1 High-Level Architecture

### 5.1.1 System Overview

#### 5.1.1.1 Architectural Style and Rationale

Dnsmasq implements a **single-threaded event-driven architecture** with poll-based I/O multiplexing, representing a deliberate design choice optimized for resource-constrained embedded deployments and small network environments. This architectural approach delivers several critical advantages:

**Concurrency Without Threads**: The event-driven model eliminates synchronization complexity, lock contention, and race conditions inherent in multi-threaded designs. By multiplexing all I/O operations through a single poll() system call, dnsmasq achieves concurrent handling of hundreds of clients without threading overhead or context switching costs.

**Predictable Performance**: Single-threaded execution provides deterministic performance characteristics crucial for embedded systems. Memory consumption remains bounded and predictable, with no unpredictable garbage collection pauses or thread stack allocation overhead. CPU utilization scales linearly with request rate, enabling accurate capacity planning.

**Minimal Resource Footprint**: The architecture targets devices with as little as 8-16MB of total RAM and single-core embedded processors (ARM Cortex-A series, MIPS cores). A typical deployment consumes 1-2MB resident memory with default configuration, scaling to 5-10MB with larger caches and lease databases.

**Fork-Based Isolation**: Blocking operations (TCP connections, script execution) are isolated in forked child processes, preventing main event loop blockage while maintaining architectural simplicity. The OS manages child process lifecycle and resource limits, eliminating the need for complex thread pool management.

#### 5.1.1.2 Key Architectural Principles

**Portability Through Abstraction**: The codebase maintains strict separation between portable protocol logic and platform-specific system interfaces. Platform differences are encapsulated in dedicated modules (`src/netlink.c` for Linux, `src/bpf.c` for BSD, platform-specific socket options) with conditional compilation based on feature detection macros defined in `src/config.h`.

**Modular Compilation**: Feature flags (HAVE_DNSSEC, HAVE_DHCP, HAVE_TFTP, etc.) enable compile-time feature selection, allowing builders to create customized binaries ranging from minimal 100KB builds for severely constrained devices to full-featured 500KB builds with all capabilities enabled.

**Zero External Dependencies**: The core functionality operates with only libc, requiring no databases, message queues, or external services. Optional features gracefully degrade when dependencies (libdbus, nettle, libidn2, libnftables) are unavailable, maintaining base functionality.

**Explicit Resource Management**: Manual memory management with custom allocators (`src/util.c:whine_malloc()`, `src/util.c:safe_malloc()`) provides deterministic allocation behavior. Cache sizes, forwarding table dimensions, and lease limits are explicitly configured, preventing unbounded memory growth.

#### 5.1.1.3 System Boundaries and Major Interfaces

**Northbound Interfaces** (Client-Facing Services):

- **DNS Service**: UDP and TCP listeners on port 53 handling DNS queries from downstream clients with forwarding, caching, and local resolution capabilities
- **DHCPv4 Service**: UDP listener on port 67 providing IPv4 address allocation and lease management with BOOTP backwards compatibility
- **DHCPv6 Service**: UDP listener on port 547 providing IPv6 address allocation, prefix delegation, and stateless configuration
- **TFTP Service**: UDP listener on port 69 providing read-only file transfer for network boot scenarios
- **Router Advertisement**: ICMPv6 multicast providing IPv6 prefix information and SLAAC support

**Southbound Interfaces** (Upstream Dependencies):

- **Upstream DNS Resolvers**: UDP/TCP connections to recursive DNS servers listed in `/etc/resolv.conf` or manually configured
- **Lease Database**: File-based persistent storage at `/var/lib/misc/dnsmasq.leases` (platform-specific paths)
- **Configuration Files**: `/etc/dnsmasq.conf` primary configuration, `/etc/hosts` local resolution, `/etc/dnsmasq.d/*.conf` modular configuration
- **Trust Anchors**: `/etc/dnsmasq.d/trust-anchors.conf` for DNSSEC root key validation

**Lateral Interfaces** (System Integration):

- **D-Bus Control**: System bus service `uk.org.thekelleys.dnsmasq` providing programmatic cache management, metrics retrieval, and configuration queries
- **Netlink/BPF**: Kernel interface for real-time network interface monitoring, address change notifications, and routing table updates
- **Ipset/Nftables**: Firewall integration for dynamic IP set population based on DNS resolution results
- **Syslog**: Asynchronous logging queue with configurable facility (default LOG_DAEMON) for operational visibility
- **Script Execution**: Fork/exec of external scripts on DHCP lease events, TFTP transfers, and authentication operations

### 5.1.3 Data Flow Description

#### 5.1.3.1 DNS Query Processing Flow

**Cache Hit Path** (Optimized Fast Path):

The DNS query processing begins when a client query arrives on port 53 (UDP or TCP). The `receive_query()` function in `src/forward.c` performs initial validation of the DNS packet structure using `src/rfc1035.c:extract_request()` to parse the wire format, extracting the query name, type (A, AAAA, CNAME, PTR, etc.), and class (typically IN for Internet).

The cache lookup operation (`src/cache.c:cache_find_by_name()`) searches the LRU cache structure, which integrates three data sources: upstream DNS responses cached with TTL tracking, `/etc/hosts` file entries loaded at startup and monitored via inotify for changes, and DHCP lease hostname registrations injected by `src/lease.c:lease_update_dns()`. For cache hits with valid TTL, the response is constructed in-memory by `src/rfc1035.c:setup_reply()` and transmitted directly to the client within sub-millisecond latency.

**Cache Miss Path** (Upstream Forwarding):

Cache misses trigger the upstream forwarding state machine. The forwarder allocates a forwarding record (frec) from the fixed-size forwarding table (default 150 entries, FTABSIZ in `src/config.h`), assigns a new randomized query ID to prevent response spoofing, and applies 0x20 bit randomization by mixed-casing the query name for additional entropy. The server selection algorithm (`src/forward.c:server_select()`) chooses an upstream resolver from `daemon->serverarray` based on query domain, previous server health, and configured domain-specific routing rules.

The query is transmitted from a randomly selected source port (configurable range, default system-assigned from 1024-65535) to the upstream server with a 10-second timeout (TIMEOUT constant). The forwarder registers the source socket with the event loop via `poll_listen()` and returns control, allowing other operations to proceed concurrently.

**Response Processing and Cache Population**:

When the upstream response arrives, `src/forward.c:reply_query()` validates the response ID, checks for truncation (TC bit) requiring TCP retry, and optionally invokes `src/dnssec.c:dnssec_validate()` for cryptographic verification if DNSSEC is enabled. Valid responses undergo address extraction by `src/rfc1035.c:extract_addresses()`, which parses A/AAAA records in the answer section.

If ipset or nftables integration is configured, `src/ipset.c:ipset_add()` or `src/nftset.c:nftset_add()` populates kernel firewall sets with resolved IP addresses via netlink. The cache population operation (`src/cache.c:cache_insert()`) adds records to the LRU cache with TTL expiration tracking, potentially evicting the least recently used entry if the cache is full.

Finally, `src/rfc1035.c:setup_reply()` reconstructs the response with the original query ID restored, applies the original query name casing pattern, and transmits to all waiting clients (multiple clients may have issued identical queries during the upstream lookup, tracked via the frec structure).

#### 5.1.3.2 DHCP Lease Allocation Flow

**Discovery and Context Matching**:

DHCPv4 packet reception occurs through platform-specific mechanisms: Linux uses IP_PKTINFO socket option to receive destination address and interface information, while BSD uses BPF raw sockets for packet capture. The `src/dhcp.c:dhcp_packet()` function parses the DHCP message structure per RFC 2131, extracting the MAC address (chaddr field), requested IP address (option 50), hostname (option 12), and vendor/user class identifiers.

Context matching via `src/dhcp.c:complete_context()` determines which DHCP address pool serves this request based on the receiving interface, relay agent IP (giaddr field), and network segment. The tag system (`src/dhcp.c:match_netid()`) evaluates conditional rules based on vendor class, user class, MAC address patterns, and previous tag assignments, selecting applicable DHCP options for this client.

**Address Selection Algorithm**:

For static reservations, `src/dhcp.c:config_find_by_address()` searches for explicit MAC-to-IP mappings defined via dhcp-host directives. For dynamic allocation, `src/dhcp.c:address_allocate()` implements a deterministic selection algorithm: the SDBM hash function computes a hash of the client's MAC address, mapping to an offset within the available address range to provide stable address assignment across renewals.

The ping cache (`src/dhcp.c:do_icmp_ping()`) maintains a 30-second validity window (PING_CACHE_TIME) for recently verified addresses. If the selected address is not in the ping cache, dnsmasq sends an ICMP echo request with a 3-second timeout (PING_WAIT) to detect conflicts with statically configured hosts or rogue DHCP clients. Ping responses or DHCP DECLINE messages trigger a 600-second backoff (DECLINE_BACKOFF) before the address is considered available again.

**Lease Commitment and Integration**:

Upon successful address selection, `src/lease.c:lease_allocate()` creates or updates the lease record in memory, setting the expiration timestamp based on configured lease time (default 3600 seconds, DEFLEASE). The lease database write operation `src/lease.c:lease_update_file()` persists the lease to `/var/lib/misc/dnsmasq.leases` in the format:

```
<expiry_timestamp> <mac_address> <ip_address> <hostname> <client_id>
```

The DNS integration `src/lease.c:lease_update_dns()` injects the DHCP hostname into the DNS cache, making the newly assigned client immediately resolvable by other network clients without additional configuration.

If lease-change scripts are configured, `src/helper.c:queue_event()` enqueues a script execution event. The helper process (`src/helper.c:helper_main()`) forks a child process with the configured script UID/GID, sets environment variables (DNSMASQ_LEASE_ACTION=add, DNSMASQ_CLIENT_MAC, DNSMASQ_IP_ADDRESS, etc.), and executes the script with a 150-second lifetime limit (CHILD_LIFETIME).

Finally, `src/rfc2131.c:dhcp_reply()` constructs the DHCPOFFER or DHCPACK response with the assigned IP address, subnet mask, default gateway, DNS servers, and requested DHCP options, transmitting via the appropriate interface using broadcast or unicast based on client capabilities.

#### 5.1.3.3 Configuration Reload Flow

**Signal Reception and Event Queuing**:

SIGHUP signal reception triggers `src/dnsmasq.c:sig_handler()`, which writes EVENT_RELOAD to the internal signal pipe. The signal pipe (created via `src/dnsmasq.c:event_pipe()`) uses the self-pipe trick for async-signal-safe notification: the write end is accessed from signal context, while the read end is monitored by the main event loop via `poll_listen()`.

**Cache and State Management**:

The main event loop detects the readable signal pipe, calls `src/dnsmasq.c:async_event()` to read the event code, and invokes `src/dnsmasq.c:clear_cache_and_reload()`. This function increments the SOA serial number for authoritative zones, then calls `src/cache.c:cache_start_insert()` to begin cache clearing. The cache clear operation preserves DHCP-derived entries (those inserted via `lease_update_dns()`) to maintain lease-to-hostname mappings, while removing all upstream DNS entries to ensure fresh data.

**Configuration Reparse and Server List Rebuild**:

The reload sequence calls `src/option.c:reread_dhcp()` to reparse DHCP configuration files, potentially updating dhcp-host entries, dhcp-range definitions, and tag-based option sets. The `src/forward.c:reload_servers()` function re-reads `/etc/resolv.conf` to detect upstream DNS server changes, rebuilding `daemon->serverarray` if modifications are detected.

The hosts file reload `src/cache.c:cache_reload()` uses inotify-based change detection on Linux to determine if `/etc/hosts` has been modified. If changed, the entire hosts file is reparsed and reloaded into the cache with the HOSTS flag set to distinguish from DNS cache entries.

**Listener Adjustment and Service Resumption**:

If the listening interface configuration has changed (--interface, --except-interface, --listen-address directives), `src/network.c:check_servers()` closes obsolete listeners and creates new listeners via `src/network.c:create_bound_listeners()`. In bind-dynamic mode, listeners are adjusted without service interruption as interface addresses change.

The reload completes with zero packet loss—in-flight DNS queries continue processing with their original forwarding state, DHCP transactions complete normally, and new queries use the updated configuration. The entire reload sequence completes within 100 milliseconds typical, maintaining the design principle of hot reconfiguration without service interruption.
